text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.3% today, extending a sharp two-week decline of 11%. The drop follows the company's quarterly earnings announcement on November 5th and coincides with a significant shift in political risk: midterm elections delivered what was widely described as a "blue wave rebuke" of Trump and the GOP, which raises the prospect of stronger renewable energy policies and potentially tighter environmental regulation on oil producers going forward.

The immediate pressure also reflects softer crude fundamentals — US oil prices have drifted down to roughly $99.60 per barrel, creating a headwind for refining margins and cash flow at a major producer. While geopolitical tensions with Iran remain unresolved (and could theoretically tighten supply later), the near-term narrative is dominated by political uncertainty around energy policy and a modest retreat in oil prices from earlier peaks.
